title: Factorized layer x input-block rotation codes for groupwise int4
hypothesis: A layer factor shared across the two projections in a layer, composed with an input-block factor shared across layers, can approach independent per-matrix/block int4 reconstruction while storing substantially fewer rotation bytes.
physical_object: 12 Pythia-70M attention-dense and MLP-up matrices from layers 0-5, input width 512
mirror_coordinate: Composition of one layer-indexed and one input-block-indexed exact signed-permutation factor around a fixed 32D Hadamard basis
logical_multiplicity: Different effective per-layer/per-block quantization gauges reconstructed from shared factors

code_search.code_family: exact 32D Hadamard followed by a signed permutation
code_search.factor_fit: two fixed coordinate-descent sweeps on training-layer calibration rows only; choose layer factor IDs then block factor IDs

development.selection_metric: held-out-layer relative Frobenius NRMSE, actual full payload bytes, rotation-only bytes, exact native alias

controls: independent selected code per matrix x input block
layer-shared selected code per layer x input block
fitted factorized layer x block codes
native BOFT-style shared-factor selection using the same factor family

paid_objects: every selected independent rotation code or factor codebook and factor ID

success_gate: Both dev seeds: factorized held-out NRMSE <=1.05x independent matrix-block control; rotation bytes at least 50% lower and total payload at least 0.05% lower than independent; no exact native factor-selection alias.
failure_gate: Any quality or byte gate miss, or exact alias to the native BOFT-style factor-selection control.
boundaries: Matrix reconstruction only; no language NLL/perplexity claim
Exact orthogonal gauges are not new functional capacity
Fresh seeds remain sealed after any dev gate miss or native alias
